back: A microprocessor-based system with a dedicated function, built into a larger device.
A computer (PC, laptop) that runs many different programs for many tasks.
The fixed program stored in ROM or flash memory that controls an embedded system.

front: Five areas that use embedded systems
back: Domestic appliances, cars, security systems, lighting systems, vending machines.
Dedicated function; part of a larger device; small, cheap, low power; fixed firmware; often real time; simple interface.
Embedded: one job, fixed firmware, simple interface. General-purpose: many tasks, user installs software, full interface.
Hard to upgrade; whole unit may need replacing if it fails; internet-connected ones can be hacked.

front: Why real time matters in a car
back: Airbags and anti-lock brakes must respond to sensor readings immediately; any delay could cause an accident.
A single chip with a processor, memory and input/output connections, used in many embedded systems.
